title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
abstract: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget; database-backed agents must keep context current, selective, traceable. Architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, ElastiCache for Valkey, Neptune, and Bedrock AgentCore. How agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, discover MCP tools. Freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, compaction. favorites lens: context-window economy + Valkey + skills + MCP is the exact haunting stack.

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of DAT443-R. Context engineering for database-backed agents across Aurora, ElastiCache Valkey, Neptune, and Bedrock AgentCore: caching, retrieval, freshness, provenance, compaction.

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of DAT443-R. Context engineering for database-backed agents: caching, retrieval, freshness, provenance, compaction across Aurora, Valkey, Neptune, AgentCore.

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. Use Kiro, AWS's AI-powered development environment, to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode team conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one. favorites lens: Kiro steering files + MCP + subagents, the haunting's exact configuration.

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of AIM301-R. Kiro steering files, MCP servers, and subagents to recover tribal knowledge into living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases.

title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
abstract: How Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge, and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent's memory lifecycle. Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes (successful build commands, rejected pull requests), consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, retrieves only relevant context. How provenance keeps memories auditable, how memory stays consistent across IDE/CLI/web, how AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes. favorites lens: Kiro session-to-memory lifecycle, directly the session-continuity concern.

title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. Build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents: RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering.

title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
abstract: Can your agents explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. Use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph any agent framework can query. AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, one rule update propagates across every agent, each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace.

title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
abstract: AI agents assert relationships (compatible products, cleared counterparties, approved suppliers) derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When wrong, downstream decisions fail. Implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer: before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, the graph data model for authoritative relationship data. favorites lens: graph-verified agent guardrails, the validation-gate pattern.

title: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
abstract: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships. Agentic GraphRAG lets agents autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use. Build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit: transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools so agents answer multi-faceted questions needing context from multiple knowledge sources.

title: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
abstract: LLMs pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, causing subtle failures on enterprise data. Ontologies give AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, what questions are meaningful. Build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources.

title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are hard to investigate without a structured provenance layer. Design an agent observability system using DynamoDB for the operational audit log and Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, how those conclusions shaped the output. favorites lens: explainable agent provenance, the OTEL-monitor concern in graph form.

title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously, reasoning at the specification level not the code level? Encoding structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context is lost, agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Distinguished (500). favorites lens: spec-level autonomy + validation signals, the spec-discipline concern.

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to conducting research alongside you? AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, run experiments autonomously. The compositional architecture, graph-routed retrieval achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and an agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Distinguished (500). favorites lens: multi-agent research orchestration, the haunting's research-analyst pattern.

title: How Blue Origin built a centralized enterprise knowledge graph on AWS
abstract: Building enterprise AI shouldn't require every team to reinvent data pipelines, security, and knowledge bases. Blue Origin faced this at scale: dozens of teams, hundreds of data sources. The answer was RAGNet, a centralized enterprise knowledge graph platform on Amazon Neptune and Amazon Bedrock that aggregates structured and unstructured data into a secure, always-current graph any developer or AI agent can query in plain natural language. space-satellite lens: Blue Origin.

title: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
abstract: Organized fraud rings exploit gaps between siloed detection systems, invisible to rules-based approaches. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, train an ensemble combining transaction-foundation-model embeddings with graph embeddings. Deploy a multi-agent system on Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, creates validated detection rules. Real-estate lens: the fraud/integrity move, duplicate-listing and synthetic-identity rings mapped as graphs.

title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. Build a knowledge assistant across all of it on Amazon Bedrock: Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion for PDFs and images, natural-language querying over structured data, GraphRAG for questions spanning connected entities. Make it enterprise-ready with tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop cited answers.

title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems each handoff can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. Build a real-time graph answering: who are my agents, what can each do, what can they reach through each other? Connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. favorites lens: multi-agent privilege monitoring, the dispatch-security concern.

title: Teaching Quick to Remember and Connect with Memory and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Amazon Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph connecting people, projects, decisions, and evidence. Architecture and tradeoffs: memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, agents that get better over time.

title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
abstract: Organizations that moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what changed, what was already decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to organized, accessible data: trust every answer back to source, prove every decision with an audit trail, synthesize intelligence across systems.
